GOAL: check the Poincaré-drift specification for faithfulness to the idea and for mathematical correctness (lift, log/exp, Mobius sum, displacement, distance scale, gradient path, switches).
READ: the idea text/equations/ablations and the full specification dict (mechanism, computations, conventions, continuous_surface, switches, excluded, gradient_rules).
OBSERVED / REASONED:
1) Lift: tanhc(sqrt(c)||r||/q)*(r/q) = (1/sqrt(c))*tanh(sqrt(c)||r||/q)*r/||r|| — identical to the idea. OK.
2) Mobius addition and the c->0 limits (v=r/q, Δ=(m/2)n, distance 2||x-y||, vector addition) are internally consistent; displacement Δ=exp_0((m/2)n) does have d_c(0,Δ)=m exactly under the (2/sqrt(c)) metric. OK.
3) LOG FORMULA DEFECT: behaviour_tangent writes log_x^c(y) = (2/(sqrt(c)*lambda_x^c))*atanhc(sqrt(c)||w||)*w with w=(-x)(+)y — no division by ||w||. With atanhc(a)=artanh(a)/a this equals (2/(c*lambda_x))*artanh(...)*w/||w||, i.e. a factor 1/sqrt(c) too large. Numerically (c=0.25, v=0.3) it returns 2v instead of v, so it violates the spec's own identity log_0^c(exp_0^c(v))=v and has no finite c->0 limit, contradicting switch_geometry's claim that the euclid branch keeps the behaviour field unchanged.
4) GRADIENT PATH: the idea says "gradients flow only through v_i and u_k"; loss_total says NO term in C or q enters the loss (cost = decision variable) and the mechanism says that claim is withdrawn — a change of the idea; meanwhile sinkhorn_plan, nearest_code_distance and arc_length are marked differentiable:true and arc_length's own note says no gradient runs through m_i; loss_total also keeps "plus whatever plan term the baseline already has", which would carry C's gradient. Contradictory/undefined gradient path.
5) SCALE: behaviour_magnitude uses M_i = lambda_{v_i}||t_i|| (>=2||t_i||) while the idea's raw magnitude is ||t_i||; m_i and the displacement are inflated by >=2 (unbounded near the boundary).
6) SCALE: poincare_cost uses (2/sqrt(c))*artanh, twice the idea's (1/sqrt(c))*artanh; with the baseline epsilon unchanged this halves the entropic temperature and changes the plan ("changes no argmin" only covers an argmin, which the mechanism never takes).
OPEN: none — verdict REVISE with four findings, each with a spec-only test.

Goal: review the Poincare displacement specification against the idea. Read: the specification in the task (mechanism, computations, conventions, gradient_rules, switches, continuous_surface) and the two leftover files in unverified/ (a previous math_review and an execution record) for structure only. Observed: (1) the level-3 work is coherent with the factor-2 metric convention (exp_0, log_x, d_c and lambda_x are mutually consistent, so d_c(0,exp_0^c(v)) = 2||v|| and the displacement entry is correct); (2) BUT computations.successor_snapshot defines r_{s,3} = z_s - E_{k_2(s)}, dropping the level-1 codeword, although level_residual gives r_{i,3} = z_i - E_{k_1} - E_{k_2}; (3) the GEOM switch changes the lift as well as the metric and never fixes whether Delta_i is built at c=1, so 'differ in the METRIC only' is false; (4) the (2/sqrt c) amendment is justified only by the plan's temperature, not by the doubling of the displacement's arc length and the moved clip threshold; (5) the mechanism claims the gradient reaches 'the displacement's parameters' while Delta_i/m_i/n_i are declared detached; (6) the residual-chain detach makes v_i a constant at levels 2 and 3, contradicting the cost gradient rule and the differentiable:true flags; (7) the mechanism says C is fed 'unchanged into the baseline's Sinkhorn' while sinkhorn_plan says the baseline rescales distances to [-1,1] first. Open: nothing; verdict REVISE.

Complete answer (verdict REVISE, six findings, each with a spec test):
{"verdict": "REVISE", "findings": ["computations.successor_snapshot: the level-3 snapshot residual is written r_{s,3} = z_s - E_{k_2(s)}, which omits the level-1 codeword, although this same spec defines r_{i,l} = z_i - sum_{j<l} E_{k_j(i)} and level_residual therefore gives r_{i,3} = z_i - E_{k_1(i)} - E_{k_2(i)}. As written V_3[s] is the ball point of a level-2 residual, so the level-3 successor points, the level-3 tangent t_i and the level-3 displacement of the codes are all built from the wrong point. It must be r_{s,3} = z_s - E_{k_1(s)} - E_{k_2(s)} with BOTH indices the epoch-start ones.", "computations.switch_geometry / switches: the switch sets c := 0, replaces the lift exp_0^c(r/q_l) by the linear r/q_l, replaces Mobius addition by vector addition, keeps the behaviour field and the cap d_nn_i at c = 1, and still claims 'the two arms differ in the METRIC only' and that the Euclidean arm 'displaces the codes exactly as the curved arm does'. Both claims are false as stated: (i) the linear lift gives different cost arguments v_i and u_k than the curved lift, so the field's d_nn_i, m_i and Delta_i are computed at points the cost never uses and the cap no longer caps anything in the metric of the cost; (ii) computations.displacement takes c as an input, so in the Euclidean arm Delta_i = exp_0^c((m_i/2) n_i) collapses to (m_i/2) n_i instead of the curved tanh(sqrt(c) m_i/2)/sqrt(c) n_i, and the codes are not displaced as in the curved arm. The switch must state that the lift, the Mobius addition and the displacement are all taken as the c -> 0 limit (and the field recomputed at c = 0), or keep the curved points and the curved Delta_i in both arms and change the distance only; 'metric only' cannot hold with a changed lift.", "conventions.distance / computations.displacement: the prefactor is changed from the idea's (1/sqrt(c)) artanh to (2/sqrt(c)) artanh and the amendment is justified only by the entropy of the plan. The same factor doubles the geodesic length of the displacement: under the idea's metric d_c(0, Delta_i) = m_i/2, under the amended metric d_c(0, Delta_i) = m_i, so the codes move twice as far for the same raw magnitude M_i and the clip m_i = min(M_i, 0.5*d_nn_i) starts biting at M_i > 0.5*d_nn_i instead of M_i > d_nn_i. The spec must either keep the idea's 1/sqrt(c) prefactor or state this second consequence and make the clip/step consistent with it (halve the step or cap at 0.25*d_nn_i).", "mechanism vs computations.displaced_code and gradient_rules: the mechanism says 'the reconstruction's gradient reaches the cost, and through it the item point v_i, the codebook rows u_k and the displacement's parameters', but Delta_i, m_i and n_i are declared detached constants ('no gradient to the behaviour field', 'the behaviour field ... rule: no gradient', 'BOTH terms of the clip detached'). There are no differentiable displacement parameters; the sentence must name only C, u_k and v_i where the residual chain allows, and must not claim any gradient into the displacement.", "gradient_rules / computations.level_residual / computations.ball_lift: the residual-chain rule residual = (residual - quant).detach() makes r_{i,2} and r_{i,3} constants, hence v_i = exp_0^c(r_{i,l}/q_l) is a constant at both fine levels, yet the cost rule states 'the reconstruction's gradient reaches v_i, u_k', level_residual and ball_lift are marked differentiable true, and the idea req

uires the gradients to flow through v_i. At levels 2 and 3 the gradient reaches only u_k. The spec must state whether the fine-level residual chain is detached; if it is, remove v_i from the gradient path and mark level_residual/ball_lift non-differentiable for l in {2,3}; if it is not, define how r_{i,l} keeps its derivative.", "computations.sinkhorn_plan vs mechanism: the mechanism says C 'is fed unchanged into the baseline's Sinkhorn with the baseline's epsilon and marginals', while sinkhorn_plan states that the baseline's own level-3 rule first rescales its distances to [-1,1] and that the mechanism does not, so the mechanism's plan runs at a different temperature. The idea asks for 'the baseline's Sinkhorn (same epsilon, same marginals, same extraction)', and a global rescale of C is exactly a change of epsilon, so 'same epsilon' is not honoured.
